newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan traders worry over missing Thai sugar.
newsitem.headline: Japan traders worry over missing Thai sugar.

text.p: Japanese traders say they are becoming increasingly worried about discrepancies in sugar cargoes shipped from Thailand.
The traders said that up to three percent of the shipments have been missing when they arrived at Japanese ports.

"We are afraid we have suffered big shortages. Of course, these shortages are somewhat covered by insurance, but the insurance is increased to the extent of the shortages..." said a letter by the Japan Sugar Import and Export Council.
The council said it prepared the letter last year, but refused to say if it was sent to Thai exporters or not. A copy of the letter was given to Reuters by a trading house source this week.
"The shortages may be due to lax loading at Bangkok ports," said a sugar trader at a major trade house said.

Japan imported 1.52 million tonnes of raw sugar in the January-November period last year, Finance Ministry data showed. Of that, 696,112 tonnes came from Thailand. -- Tokyo Commodity Desk +81-3-3432-7391
